newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate to vote at 6 p.m. EDT on budget.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate to vote at 6 p.m. EDT on budget.

text.p: The U.S. Senate will vote at 6 p.m. EDT (2200 GMT) on Monday on an omnibus spending bill for fiscal 1997 starting Oct. 1, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott announced.

"We have an agreement with the Democrats," the Mississippi Republican told reporters. Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle, D-S.D., confirmed the agreement. It assures the spending bill will pass before midnight, preventing a partial government shutdown.
The bill also includes an immigration measure and provisions to strengthen the thrift insurance fund. It passed the House overwhelmingly on Saturday.
President Clinton supports the bill and has said he will sign it before the midnight deadline.
